page: Microsoft Azure F16alds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server belonging to the Faldsv7 family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Additionally, the server is equipped with 1890 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-threaded performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores falling in the average category. Memory performance is robust, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25%, while large-block memory read and write bandwidths remain average. The processor's instruction set supports advanced vector extensions (AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F16alds_v7 provides high compute density and substantial local storage capacity relative to its memory footprint. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications. This server is highly suited for compute-bound workloads that benefit from high single-core clock speeds and local storage, such as batch processing, web serving, single-threaded compression tasks, and lightweight language model inference.
